programme_target.summary: The Programme ledger records the known stronger-index-range statement that at least one of zeta(5), zeta(7), ..., zeta(33) is irrational, without deriving any individual irrationality conclusion.

status_authority.statement: MATH-PROGRAMME retains current-status, scope, and promotion authority; upstream categories are source metadata only.

findings.summary: The upstream finite disjunction uses the exact four-element set {5,7,9,11}.
A nonempty intersection with the irrational-value set preserves an existential disjunction and does not select a member.
The four-index disjunction is logically stronger than the Programme baseline over odd indices 5 through 33, but the declaration contains sorry.

obligations: Do not infer irrationality of zeta(5), zeta(7), zeta(9), or zeta(11) individually.
Preserve the exact finite index set and existential quantifier.
Replay a proof independently before assigning proof effect.
claim_boundary: This record identifies a stronger finite disjunction at the statement level only. It does not prove that disjunction, select an irrational value, or create a new Programme theorem claim.
